# Flipper UI from the design, with Auto-save new

## Overview
- Rebuild the Flipper app's screens after the Claude Design page "FliBuddy
  Flipper" (reference: `docs/design/flipper/flipper-ui.js`, the prototype's
  renderer and state machine, and the distilled spec below).
- Add the Flipper setting **Auto-save new** (default **Off**). On: a scanned
  Bambu tag that Bambuddy does not know is created at once with defaults, and
  the Flipper shows "Added to Bambuddy" with OK = Weigh for a started spool.
  Off: nothing reaches Bambuddy until the owner presses **Add** (OK on the
  result, "Add new" in the menu) or saves a weight ("Add and weigh", or the
  host's Save / New). This replaces today's unconditional create-on-scan.
- Add the known-spool actions **Mark as new** (remaining = label weight),
  **Mark as empty** (remaining 0 and archived), both with a 3 s Undo before anything is sent, and
  **Delete spool** behind a confirmation screen.
- Add LED / vibro / sound feedback per event, with Feedback and Sound
  settings.
- The host now sends structured spool fields so the Flipper lays the
  screens out itself; protocol version goes to 2.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-26)
- Auto-save new lives on the Flipper (its Settings). The flag travels in every
  `scan`; the host obeys it. Hosts get no separate switch: their feed shows
  either a created row or a row waiting for New / Save.
- Default Off.
- In scope from the design: base flow (Waiting, Ready / Next spool, Reading,
  Result for known / unknown / blank, Menu, Tag details, Weight with net/gross,
  Saving, Saved, toasts, Link on host, Error, Settings, About), Mark as new /
  empty with Undo, Delete with confirmation, LED / vibro / sound.
- Out of scope now: the **Recent** screen (Ready's ◀ does nothing), the
  settings **After scan** and **Weigh as**, the design's **Connection = Auto**
  (keep USB / Bluetooth; the Waiting screen shows the one transport in use).
- Protocol: the host sends structured fields; `lines` stay for errors and as
  a fallback. Version bumps, Flipper and hosts ship together.
- Earlier rules still hold: idempotent intents keyed by id, rescans change
  nothing, known spools get weights at once, Mac rows strictly newest first,
  a rescan moves the row to the top.

- **CRITICAL: all tests must pass before starting the next task.**

## Flipper UI spec (distilled from the design)

Screen 128×64, 1 bit. OK always does the screen's main action, ◀ opens the
menu or cancels, ▶ is the quick second action, Back goes back. Bottom row
holds up to three rounded "button" chips: ◀ label (left), OK label (centre),
label ▶ (right), drawn inverted. Titles bold at the top with a dotted rule
under them; the transport icon (USB or Bluetooth) sits top right on every
screen that has a header; the Bluetooth icon blinks while advertising without
a host. Use the firmware fonts (FontPrimary for titles, FontSecondary for
body, FontBigNumbers for the weight digits) and XBM icons generated from the
bitmaps in `flipper-ui.js` (`I.usb`, `I.bt`, `I.check`, `I.warn`, arrows,
`I.app` for the 10×10 app icon). Pixel positions in `flipper-ui.js` are the
target; small shifts to fit the firmware fonts are fine.

Screens (keys: OK / ◀ / ▶ / ▲▼ / Back):
1. **Waiting for host** — title "FliBuddy" + version; line for the active
   transport ("USB: no host app" / "Bluetooth: visible as <name>" / "Bluetooth
   off"); "Waiting for host…" animated. ▶ Settings, Back exits.
2. **Ready** — spool picture with animated waves, "Ready", "Hold spool tag to
   the back". After a save / add / mark: inverted bar with the last outcome
   ("Saved PLA Basic 590 g", "Added PLA Silk+", "New PLA 1000 g", "Empty PLA",
   "Deleted PLA") and "Next spool". ▶ Settings, ◀ none, Back exits.
3. **Reading tag** — spool + waves, "Keep still". No keys.
4. **Looking up** — while the lookup is pending (no timeout, as today); Back
   to Ready. Not in the design; keep it minimal (title + material from the tag
   if parsed locally, else "Looking up").
5. **Result · known** — colour swatch (Bayer-dithered by luminance of the
   spool RGBA) + material as title; colour name (or `Color #RRGGBB`);
   `Tag 91B4…E7C2`; `590 g left of 1000`. OK Weigh, ▶ New (Mark as new),
   ◀ Menu, Back Ready.
6. **Result · unknown Bambu** (Auto-save Off) — swatch + material; colour;
   UID; inverted "Not in Bambuddy". OK Add, ▶ Link, ◀ Menu.
7. **Result · blank / no data** — circle + "Blank tag" / tag type; UID;
   inverted "No spool data". OK Link (asks the host), ◀ Menu.
8. **Menu** (▲▼, OK, Back to result) — known: Weigh, Mark as new, Mark as
   empty, Relink on host, Tag details, Delete spool. Unknown: Add new, Add and
   weigh, Link on host, Tag details. Blank: Link on host, Tag details. A
   no-material unknown keeps today's "Create on host" in place of Add.
9. **Tag details** — Type, UID with colons, Data, RGBA, Label g. OK/Back to menu.
10. **Delete · confirm** — warning icon, "Delete spool?", material + colour,
    "Removes it from Bambuddy for good." ◀ Cancel, ▶ Delete (far from OK);
    OK does nothing.
11. **Weight** — title "Weight", net/gross segmented chip top right; four big
    digits with dimmed leading zeros and a cursor bar under the active digit;
    the cursor's leftmost position (◀ from the first digit) is the mode chip,
    where ▲▼ toggles net/gross and an untouched pre-fill is recomputed. ◀▶
    move, ▲▼ change the digit (wraps), OK Save, Back to result. Line under
    the digits: gross → `Net 590 g · core 325`; net → `Saves 590 g left`;
    gross below core → inverted "Below core weight" and OK flashes red without
    sending. Pre-fill: gross = remaining + core (fallback label + core), net =
    remaining (fallback label). Mode starts gross and is remembered for the
    session (as today).
12. **Saving / Adding / Deleting / Updating** — title per action, material
    (· pending net g when saving), indeterminate bar, "Waiting for Bambuddy".
    10 s result timeout as today.
13. **Saved** — big check, "Saved", `PLA Basic · 590 g left`; 1.3 s, then
    Ready with the "Saved …" bar.
14. **Toast · Added to Bambuddy** — `Spool #31 · 1000 g`; OK Weigh, ▶ Next
    (Ready with "Added …" bar), Back Ready. No auto-dismiss.
15. **Toast · Marked as new** — `1000 g left · full`, 3 s progress bar
    "Next spool in 3 s"; ◀ Undo, OK Weigh, Back Ready; auto Ready after 3 s.
16. **Toast · Marked as empty** — `0 g left · archived`, same bar; ◀ Undo.
17. **Toast · Deleted** — "Tag is free to reuse", same bar, no Undo.
18. **Link on host** — "Pick the spool in FliBuddy on host", bouncing dots;
    ◀ Cancel / Back to result. When the host links, a fresh lookup for the
    same scan arrives and the screen becomes Result · known.
19. **Error** — title from the case ("Not saved", "No host reply", "Not a
    spool tag", "Host lost"), warning icon, up to three lines (host `lines`
    when present). ◀ Back, ▶ Retry (resends the same intent id when the
    failed intent is retryable; otherwise back to Ready).
20. **Settings** (▲▼ select, ◀▶ change value in place, Back saves and
    returns): Connection (USB / Bluetooth), Auto-save new (Off / On),
    Feedback (Vibro+LED / LED / Off), Sound (Off / On), Version (OK → About).
21. **About** — app icon ×2, "FliBuddy", "for Bambuddy", version, protocol
    version and firmware, current host ("Host: <app> · USB/BLE" or "not
    connected"). OK/Back to Settings.

Feedback (respecting Feedback / Sound settings):
- host connected: blue ×1 + short vibro;
- tag read: blue + short vibro;
- saved / added / marked / deleted: green + vibro;
- error and refused Save: red + long vibro;
- Feedback = LED drops vibro; Off drops both; Sound = On adds the firmware's
  success / error beeps to green / red events.

## Protocol v2 (summary; PROTOCOL.md is the source of truth after Task 1)
- `v` is `2` on every message; a receiver ignores other versions, so v1 and
  v2 peers see each other as silent (the hello carries the version; the host
  logs a clear "Flipper speaks protocol N" notice).
- `scan` gains `autosave: boolean` (required).
- `lookup` gains optional `spool`: `{id, material, subtype?, color_name?,
  rgba?, remaining, label, core, archived?}` for `found`, and `tag_info`:
  `{material?, subtype?, rgba?, label?}` for `unknown` from the parsed tag;
  and `created: true` when this lookup's spool was created on scan
  (Auto-save On). `lines` remain required (may be empty) and are what error
  screens show.
- `intent.action` adds `full` (Mark as new: remaining = label; restores an
  archived spool), `empty` (remaining 0, then archive) and `delete` (DELETE
  the spool). There is no `undo` action: Undo is local (see below). `weigh`
  on an unknown scan creates
  the spool with the tag defaults first, then records the weight ("Add and
  weigh"; the host's Save does the same). `new` stays "create from tag".
- `result` gains optional `spool` (same shape as in `lookup`) so Saved /
  toasts show the new remaining and the spool id.
- **Undo is local.** Mark as new / empty show their 3 s toast *without
  sending anything*; ◀ Undo returns to the result and nothing leaves the
  Flipper. When the bar runs out, or on OK Weigh / Back / a new tag, the
  Flipper sends `full` / `empty` and goes through the normal Busy → Saved →
  Ready path (Weigh after Mark as new sends `full` first, then opens Weight).
  This deviates from the design (the design commits at once) and is recorded
  under "Implemented differently".
- **Archived spools.** The host looks tags up with `include_archived=true`,
  so an emptied spool rescanned is still known (`spool.archived: true`, the
  result shows "archived" in place of the remaining line) and never becomes
  a duplicate. Weighing an archived spool or marking it new restores it from
  the archive first.
- **Version mismatch.** A receiver reads `v` before anything else; the host
  logs a peer speaking another version once ("Flipper speaks protocol N,
  host speaks 2") and shows it in its status; then drops the line.

## Post-Completion
**Manual verification** on the real Flipper (firmware 1.5.1) with the Mac app
over USB and Bluetooth:
- Auto-save Off: scan an unknown Bambu tag → Not in Bambuddy; Back → nothing
  created; Add → created; Add and weigh → created with the typed weight.
- Auto-save On: scan → Added to Bambuddy → OK Weigh → saved weight.
- Known spool: Weigh, Mark as new (Undo sends nothing; letting the bar run
  out saves), Mark as empty (archived in Bambuddy; rescan shows it archived,
  weighing restores it), Delete with confirmation.
- LED / vibro / sound per Feedback and Sound settings.
- Install with `ufbt launch`; restart the Mac app after the FAP (the USB node
  is re-created when the FAP starts).

## Implemented differently
- Task 1: the Python bridge's switch to protocol v2 (version 2 on every
  line, `lookup.spool`, `lookup.tag_info`, `result.spool` for `weigh` and
  `new`) landed with the fixtures, because the bridge tests compare its
  replies with the fixtures byte for byte and `make test-tools` gates Task 1.
  Until Tasks 2 and 6, `make test-flipper` and `make test-host` fail against
  the v2 fixtures, as the per-task gates allow.
- Task 1: `lookup` keeps `spool_id` (equal to `spool.id`) and `prefill`
  (equivalent to `tag_info.material`); `spool.subtype` is Bambuddy's stored
  subtype ("Basic"), and the Flipper titles a spool `material subtype`, or
  `subtype` alone when it already starts with the material. The Flipper's
  pre-fill comes from `spool.remaining + spool.core` (net: `remaining`), with
  `defaults` as the fallback. The `scan` key order is `t, v, scan_id,
  autosave, tag`.
- Task 2: the decoder is as strict as the schema about where the v2 fields
  may appear: `spool` or `created` outside `found`, `tag_info` outside
  `unknown`, `result.spool` with `ok: false`, or a `lookup.spool.id` other
  than `spool_id` drop the line as malformed. Unknown keys inside `spool`
  and `tag_info` are skipped, as everywhere else. `proto_encode_scan` takes
  the autosave flag; the app passes `false` until Tasks 3 and 4 wire the
  setting through the reducer.
- Task 3: the settings storage's `load` takes the saved_struct version to
  read, because `saved_struct_load` checks the header version and payload
  size itself; `app_settings_load` reads version 2 and falls back to the
  2-byte version 1 struct. A version 2 file with any out-of-range field
  loads the defaults as a whole (as an unknown transport did before). The
  migrated settings reach the file on the next save (a transport switch);
  nothing is written on load.
- Task 4: the reducer takes raw keys (`AppEventKey`) and owns the list
  selection, the Weight digits / cursor / touched flag and the Settings
  values, so the spec's key map is tested on the host; one `AppEventTick`
  runs out the 10 s result timeout, Saved (1.3 s) and the 3 s toasts
  (`app_timer_left_ms` feeds the progress bar). The feedback event is
  `AppState.cue`, reset by every `app_reduce` call, rather than a second
  return value. Settings are edited in place in `AppState.settings`;
  leaving Settings returns `AppEffectSwitchTransport` when the Connection
  differs from the transport in use (or that transport did not open: leaving
  Settings retries it), else `AppEffectSaveSettings` when anything changed.
  Back on Waiting / Ready returns `AppEffectExit`.
- Task 4: choices the spec left open: Waiting still reads tags and shows
  Result·NoHost (Menu: Tag details only); a tag on a pending Mark toast
  commits the mark and is not read (one intent in flight; the reader finds
  it again on the next reading screen); losing the host on a pending Mark
  toast drops the mark (nothing was sent) and shows Result·NoHost, on Busy
  it is Error·Host lost; `link_on_host` / `create_on_host` go straight to
  Link on host, whose result only stops the timeout; a fresh lookup for the
  scan is applied on Result, Menu, Details and Link on host (an `error`
  lookup never replaces a result) and ignored elsewhere; every intent error
  (host `ok: false`, timeout, send failure, host lost) is retryable with the
  same id, and ◀ / Back on it returns to the result while the host is
  there, else to Waiting / Ready; Mark as new / empty cue success when the
  toast opens and their committed result goes to Ready silently; Toast·
  Deleted's OK does nothing. Mode toggling moved from the result menu to the
  Weight mode chip.
- Task 4: the scenes and `flibuddy_app.c` (SDK code) still use the old
  reducer API, so `ufbt` does not build the FAP between Task 4 and Task 5,
  which replaces them; `make test-flipper` passes.
- Task 5: the scenes, Widget, Submenu and NumberInput are gone: one custom
  View whose locked model is a `UiFrame` (`src/ui_frame.h`), built by the
  SDK-free `ui_frame_build()` after every state change and tick and laid
  out by `src/ui_draw.c` on the GUI thread, which never reads `AppState`.
  All wording lives in the frame builder and is tested on the host
  (`tests/test_ui_frame.c`); `screen_text.{h,c}` and
  `tag_summary_text()` are replaced by `ui_text.{h,c}` and
  `tag_block_text()` / `tag_sectors_read()`.
- Task 5: the firmware fonts are ASCII only: "..." stands for the ellipsis
  (`04B7...3C80`; a 4-byte UID is shown whole) and " - " for the middle dot
  (`PLA Basic - 590 g left`, `Net 484 g - core 250`). "Ready" and "Saved"
  use FontPrimary (no double-size text font); the weight digits use
  FontBigNumbers, dimmed by a checkerboard; the bottom chips are the
  firmware's `elements_button_left/center/right`. Icons are XBM files in
  `flipper/images/`, generated from the design's bitmaps by
  `tools/fixtures/make_flipper_icons.py` (a pytest fails when they are
  stale), with a 20x20 `app_2x` for About since the canvas does not scale.
- Task 5: the reader re-arm is inside `TagReader`: it remembers the UID of
  every tag it read (a failed read too, when a tag answered) and its next
  worker first waits until that tag has left the field (three 150 ms polls
  in a row without an answer, `tag_watch.h`) or another tag answers. It
  holds on every screen that reads, Waiting and Ready included, so Back
  from a result with the spool still on the Flipper does not read it
  again; a different tag still commits a pending Mark toast.
- Task 5: wording the spec left open: Waiting shows "USB: no host app" /
  "USB unavailable", "Visible as <name>", "Bluetooth: no host app" (a
  central subscribed without a hello) or "Bluetooth off"; Looking up shows
  the tag's own detailed type or material and "Asking the host";
  Result·NoHost is titled by the tag's text or type with the bar "No host";
  an unknown tag without material is titled "Spool tag" with OK "Create";
  Tag details' Data row is "15/16 sectors" or "135 pages"; Weight in gross
  without a known core says "Core weight unknown"; error titles follow the
  failed action ("Not saved", "Not added", "Not deleted", "Not updated",
  "Not linked") or the case ("Lookup failed", "No host reply", "Host
  lost", "Not sent", "Tag not read"), and ▶ Retry is shown only when the
  intent can be resent (▶ still goes home otherwise).
- Task 5: feedback uses one static notification sequence per LED / vibro /
  sound combination (the service keeps the pointer); each wakes the
  backlight, the success vibro is short like the blue ones, and the beeps
  follow the vibro rather than overlapping it.
- Task 5: `flipper/README.md` still describes the old Idle / Transport
  screens; Task 9 rewrites it for the new UI.
- Task 6: Bambuddy's archive marker is not in this repository's captures,
  so `Spool` decodes `archived_at` (a date string) and an optional
  `archived` boolean, and `isArchived` is `archived ?? (archived_at != nil)`.
  The bodies of `POST …/archive` and `…/restore` are not read: Mark as empty
  takes its spool from the `PATCH` and sets `archived` itself, Mark as new
  and a weigh on an archived spool clear it after the restore. Mark as empty
  on a spool already archived skips the archive call; Delete of a spool
  already gone (404) counts as deleted.
- Task 6: the version mismatch reaches the status through
  `Transport.peerVersion` (the other version of the first such line on the
  connection; `WireLog` logs "Flipper speaks protocol N, host speaks 2" once
  at error and drops later lines at debug). At the hello timeout the link
  goes to `LinkState.otherVersion(N)` instead of `noAnswer`; the status bar
  shows the same sentence, with what to update as its detail.
  Only the hello timeout reads `peerVersion`: a Flipper of another version
  whose first line comes after the timeout leaves the link at `noAnswer`.
  In practice its hello comes at once (the USB node and the BLE advert exist
  only while the FAP runs), so this stays as is.
- Task 6: a `weigh` (or host Save) on an unknown tag whose create went
  through and whose weight failed leaves the row without the spool, showing
  the error; the retry finds the spool by tag and weighs it. New feed row
  statuses: `updating` (Mark / Delete in flight), `markedNew`,
  `markedEmpty`, `deleted`; an archived spool is `spool.isArchived`.
  `FeedItem` has plain phrases for them until Task 7. The Swift
  `Scan(autosave:)` defaults to `false`.
- Task 7: the host pushes a fresh `found` lookup (without `created`) after
  New, Link, and a host Save that created the spool, for every row, not
  only rows the Flipper flagged with `link_on_host` / `create_on_host`:
  the host cannot know what the Flipper shows, and the Flipper applies a
  lookup only for the scan on its screen (PROTOCOL.md, Session, reworded).
  `Session.pushes()` is an `AsyncStream<Message>`; `FlipperLink` sends its
  lines only while the Flipper is connected, drops what comes otherwise,
  and treats a push that cannot be sent like a reply (drop and reconnect).
- Task 7: a `Not in Bambuddy` Bambu row is an entry (`FeedItem.isEntry`,
  `savesNewSpool`) pre-filled with label + the Settings core weight
  (`FeedItem(_:coreWeight:)`), takes focus like Enter weight, and keeps the
  entry through Saving and an error; New and Link sit as link-style buttons
  right of the readout. `Marked as empty` and `Deleted` say "by Flipper";
  an archived spool's colour column reads "archived". The watch shows the
  entry on such a row without New / Link (not built here). Recorded in
  `docs/design/macos-ui-spec.md`.
- Task 7: the Python bridge pushes no lookup (it has no host actions), and
  its Mark as empty falls back to a 1000 g label when the spool has none,
  as its `spool.label` does.
- Task 9: `docs/design/flipper-ui-spec.md` describes the app as built (the
  wording and key map of `ui_frame.c` and `app_state.c`, the choices
  recorded above), not the design as drawn; Result · no host is its own
  screen there, so the numbers from Menu on are one higher than in the
  spec section of this plan. `app_state.h` and `ui_frame.h` point at it.
  The dated Phase 0 results in the root README keep their "Idle" wording.
